boxes.name: Pearl Harbor

shore.note: every dated work of Oʻahu’s harbours later than the year undone at the texel (4 × 4 samples, the half rule): lower works (land made later) back to their level, raise works (sea cut later) back to the reef that rims them, the drydocks of 1942–43 filled to the yard’s ground; the works, dates and shapes are Holo i ke Au’s (tools/lib/oahu-1941.mjs) and R10’s; the geologic map’s fill unit, which the Hawaiian patches also asked for, is not read here (research/bake.md)

hawaii-dot-hnl-history.title: Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation, Airports Division, Honolulu International Airport: the first 80 years, part 2 (1944–1959)
hawaii-dot-hnl-history.licence: State of Hawaiʻi publication, quoted for its dates
hawaii-dot-hnl-history.note: Naval Air Station Honolulu “was operational in late 1943 but was commissioned on January 1, 1944”; full operation for land and sea planes from 1 April 1944; in 1946 “three seaplane runways, each 1,000 feet wide with an average length of approximately 2.7 miles”

hawaii-dot-reef-runway.title: Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation, Airports Division, Honolulu International Airport history page
hawaii-dot-reef-runway.licence: State of Hawaiʻi publication, quoted for its dates
hawaii-dot-reef-runway.note: “In 1977, Runway 8R/26L or the Reef Runway was constructed as the fourth runway for Honolulu International Airport”

hawaii-gis-oahu-1938.title: Map of Oʻahu, 1938 (a U.S. Geological Survey topographic sheet), as georeferenced by the State of Hawaiʻi GIS (Historic_Maps/Oahu_1938 ImageServer)
hawaii-gis-oahu-1938.licence: State of Hawaiʻi Statewide GIS Program open data; the map itself is a public-domain federal survey

iooh-ala-wai-kewalo.title: Images of Old Hawaiʻi, posts tagged “Ala Wai Boat Harbor” (Ala Wai, Kewalo, Ala Moana, Magic Island)
iooh-ala-wai-kewalo.licence: quoted for its dates; text © its author
iooh-ala-wai-kewalo.note: the Ala Wai Drainage Canal “begun in 1921 and completed in 1928” led to “the draining and filling in of the ponds and irrigated fields of Waikīkī”; “Dredging of the Kewalo Channel began in 1924”, Kewalo Basin built in the 1920s; “In 1928, a channel was dredged through the coral reef to connect the Ala Wai Boat Harbor and the Kewalo Basin”; Ala Moana Park on dredged coral “completed in 1934”; “in 1951, a channel was dredged directly out to sea” from the boat harbour; Magic Island, “a 30-acre peninsula”, built in 1964

r10-pearl-harbor.title: Pacific Theatre research report R10, Pearl Harbor (research/R10-pearl-harbor.md), §7.2 and §11.4

usn-building-bases-1947.title: Building the Navy’s Bases in World War II, vol. II, ch. XXII, Hawaiian Area (Bureau of Yards and Docks, 1947; HyperWar transcription)
usn-building-bases-1947.note: Pearl Harbor: dredging for a turning channel round Ford Island from May 1940, the lochs deepened for moorings, Kuahua extended with the spoil from 47 acres to a 116-acre peninsula, Ford Island enlarged by seven acres for its T-wharves. Keʻehi: a dredge brought into the lagoon in February 1943 for three seaplane runways “1,000 feet wide by three miles long”, the spoil raising the land to ten feet. Kāneʻohe Bay: from September 1939, three years of dredging for the seaplane runways (11,000,000 cubic yards)
